chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim and al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, both of whom said:

When the affair of the deposed one came to an end and authority was firmly established for al-Maʾmūn, he wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام requesting that he come to Khurāsān. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام excused himself with various reasons, but al-Maʾmūn continued corresponding with him about this until he knew that there was no escape for him and that he would not desist from him.

So he عليه السلام departed, while Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was seven years old. Al-Maʾmūn wrote to him that he should not take the route of al-Jabal and Qumm, but rather go by the route of al-Baṣra, al-Ahwāz, and Fārs, until he arrived at Marw. Then al-Maʾmūn offered him the authority and the caliphate, but Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام refused. He said: then the succession to the heirship. He عليه السلام said: upon conditions that I shall stipulate to you. Al-Maʾmūn said to him: ask whatever you wish.

Al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote: 'I am entering into the ولاية of the heirship on the condition that I neither command nor forbid, nor give legal verdicts, nor judge, nor appoint, nor dismiss, nor change anything of what is already established, and that you exempt me from all of that.' Al-Maʾmūn accepted all of those terms.

He said: Yāsir narrated to me, saying: when the ʿĪd came, al-Maʾmūn sent to al-Riḍā عليه السلام asking him to ride out, attend the ʿĪd, lead the salat (prayer), and deliver the sermon. Al-Riḍā عليه السلام sent back to him: 'You know the conditions that were agreed between me and you upon entering into this matter.' Al-Maʾmūn sent again: 'I only intend by this that the hearts of the people may be reassured and that they may know your merit.' He عليه السلام continued to reply to him about that, but he insisted.

So he عليه السلام said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if you excuse me from that, it is more beloved to me; but if you do not excuse me, I will go out just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام went out.' Al-Maʾmūn said: 'Go out however you wish.' And al-Maʾmūn ordered the commanders and the people to come early to the door of Abū al-Ḥasan.

He said: Yāsir the servant narrated to me that the people sat waiting for Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in the streets and on the rooftops—men, women, and children—and the commanders and soldiers gathered at the door of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. When the sun rose, he عليه السلام stood, performed ghusl (ritual bath), wrapped himself in a white cotton turban, placing one end over his chest and one end between his shoulders, and gathered up his garments. Then he said to all his followers: 'Do as I have done.'

Then he took a staff in his hand and went out, while we were before him, and he was barefoot, having raised his trousers to the middle of the shin, with garments tucked up. When he walked, and we walked before him, he raised his head toward the sky and pronounced four takbīrs. It seemed to us that the sky and the walls were answering him, while the commanders and the people at the door had made themselves ready, put on their weapons, and adorned themselves with the finest adornment.

When we appeared before them in this manner and al-Riḍā عليه السلام came out, he paused at the door for a moment and then said: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest for what He has guided us to; Allah is the Greatest for what He has provided us of the grazing cattle; and all praise belongs to Allah for what He has tried us with.' We raised our voices with these words.

Yāsir said: Marw was shaken by weeping, clamour, and shouting when they looked at Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. The commanders fell from their mounts and cast away their footwear when they saw Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام barefoot; and he would walk, then stop at every ten steps and pronounce the takbīr three times. Yāsir said: it seemed to us that the sky, the earth, and the mountains were answering him, and Marw became one great outcry of weeping. This reached al-Maʾmūn, so al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, Dhu al-Riʾāsatayn, said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if al-Riḍā reaches the place of prayer in this manner, the people will be captivated by him; the opinion is that you should ask him to return.' So al-Maʾmūn sent to him and asked him to go back. Then Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام called for his footwear, put it on, mounted, and returned.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَاتٍ: pronouncements of 'Allāhu Akbar' during the procession
key_terms.الْخِلَافَةَ: the caliphate or supreme political authority
key_terms.الْعِيدُ: the festival day on which congregational worship was to be held
key_terms.الْمُصَلَّى: the open prayer ground for the ʿĪd prayer
key_terms.عُكَّازًا: a staff carried by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.وِلَايَةِ الْعَهْدِ: the office of heirship or succession offered by al-Maʾmūn
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَ: to lead or perform the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام accept the heirship under al-Maʾmūn, and what happened when he went out for the ʿĪd salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report narrates the journey of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام to Khurāsān under al-Maʾmūn and his acceptance of the heirship only under strict conditions that excluded any active participation in rule. It then describes the famous ʿĪd procession in which the Imam appeared in the manner of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, moving the people of Marw so deeply that al-Maʾmūn feared their attachment to him and ordered his return.
